title: 2018 Porsche 911 GT2 RS Weissach: Performance, Provenance, and Precision

scenes.headline: 700 Horsepower
scenes.narration: Power meets precision with an astounding 700 horsepower, making this machine a force to be reckoned with.

scenes.headline: Aerodynamic Engineering
scenes.narration: The GT2 RS Weissach's front air intakes are not just stylish but designed for optimal aerodynamics and cooling.

scenes.headline: Weissach Legacy
scenes.narration: This 2018 model launched as part of a limited series, boasting lightweight construction with its Weissach Package.

scenes.headline: 3.8L Turbo Flat-6
scenes.narration: Under the rear hatch, a 3.8-liter twin-turbocharged flat-six powers this beast, delivering 553 lb-ft of torque to the rear wheels.

scenes.headline: Rear-Wheel Drive
scenes.narration: Power is harnessed through a seven-speed PDK dual-clutch automatic transmission, all directed to the rear wheels for a pure driving experience.

scenes.headline: GT2 RS vs. Performante
scenes.narration: In a showdown with the 2018 Lamborghini Huracán Performante, the GT2 RS offers 700 hp against the Performante’s 640.

scenes.headline: Holds Its Value
scenes.narration: Sold for $695,000, this model holds significant value with its exclusive features, showing minimal depreciation from its original price.

scenes.headline: Racing Interior
scenes.narration: Inside, a red-faced chrono stopwatch takes center stage, emphasizing the car's racing heritage.

scenes.headline: Your Turn
scenes.narration: With intense power and design, could the GT2 RS Weissach be your ultimate track machine?

script: Power meets precision with an astounding 700 horsepower, making this machine a force to be reckoned with. The GT2 RS Weissach's front air intakes are not just stylish but designed for optimal aerodynamics and cooling. This 2018 model launched as part of a limited series, boasting lightweight construction with its Weissach Package. Under the rear hatch, a 3.8-liter twin-turbocharged flat-six powers this beast, delivering 553 lb-ft of torque to the rear wheels. Power is harnessed through a seven-speed PDK dual-clutch automatic transmission, all directed to the rear wheels for a pure driving experience. In a showdown with the 2018 Lamborghini Huracán Performante, the GT2 RS offers 700 hp against the Performante’s 640. Sold for $695,000, this model holds significant value with its exclusive features, showing minimal depreciation from its original price. Inside, a red-faced chrono stopwatch takes center stage, emphasizing the car's racing heritage. With intense power and design, could the GT2 RS Weissach be your ultimate track machine?

sections.Highlights: THIS... is a 2018 Porsche 911 GT2 RS Weissach, finished in Guards Red with a black interior. The odometer on this 911 GT2 RS currently displays approximately 3,900 miles. The attached Carfax history report lists no accidents or mileage discrepancies in this Porsche's past. According to the build sheet provided in the gallery, notable factory equipment includes the Weissach Package, 20-inch front and 21-inch rear magnesium wheels, PCCBs, a front axle lift system, an extended range fuel tank, leather and Alcantara upholstery, carbon fiber full bucket seats, and a Bose sound system. Notable modifications reported by the selling dealer are limited to black-finished brake calipers. Launched for 2018 as a limited-edition model, the 991-based GT2 RS stood proud as the most powerful road-going 911 ever released. Porsche went to significant lengths to make the model as light as possible -- it notably fitted lighter springs, numerous carbon fiber parts, and cloth interior door handles. The optional Weissach Package -- which this car is equipped with -- saved an additional 40 pounds. Most sources agree that Porsche built around 1,000 units of the 991-based 911 GT2 RS. Power comes from a twin-turbocharged 3.8-liter flat-6, rated at 700 horsepower and 553 lb-ft of torque. Output is sent to the rear wheels via a 7-speed PDK dual-clutch automatic transmission.
sections.Equipment: A build sheet is provided in the photo gallery, and a partial list of notable equipment reported by the seller includes: Weissach Package Chrono Package with preparation for Lap Trigger 20-inch front and 21-inch rear magnesium wheels in black Porsche Ceramic Composite Brakes (PCCB) Front axle lift system Rear axle steering Extended range fuel tank Leather and Alcantara upholstery Carbon fiber full bucket seats Bose sound system
sections.Seller Notes: The selling dealer notes that the paint protection film has been applied to exterior panels. The selling dealer states that the magnesium wheels were uninstalled early in the vehicle's life and have been reinstalled in preparation for the sale, and that its Michelin Pilot Sport Cup 2 tires have about 9/32 of tread.
